name: Fellowship Bible Church Tucson
summary: Six 2026 sermons by senior pastor Pat McClanahan map one-to-one onto same-titled sermons from Alistair Begg's Truth For Life series. Measured against the sermon body rather than the full livestream, 10% to 40% of each sermon falls inside near-verbatim reused regions (27.2% across the six sermons); Begg and Truth For Life were not named in any of the six sermons.

pastors.name: Pat McClanahan

plagiarism.summary: All six reviewed 2026 sermons preached by Pat McClanahan in the 1 Thessalonians series track one same-titled Alistair Begg sermon. Sermon-body coverage ranges from 10% to 40%, with 27.2% of the six sermons inside near-verbatim reused regions (25.0% after shared Scripture is removed). Full-transcript review found no spoken mention of Alistair Begg or Truth For Life in any of the six sermons.

evidence.description: Near-verbatim reused regions cover 20% of the 44-minute sermon body. The sermon follows Begg's outline and carries across commentary, illustrations, the closing line, and a closing prayer while replacing some local details.

Near-verbatim reused regions cover 40% of the sermon body, the highest share in the six-sermon set. The review found the same outline, word studies, commentator material, applications, and closing formulation in the same order.

Near-verbatim reused regions cover 39% of the sermon body. The review identifies carried-over commentary, a John Stott quotation framed as the FBC preacher's own reading, the same outline, and matching applications.

Near-verbatim reused regions cover 36% of the sermon body. The longest detected non-Scripture region runs 361 words, and the sermon carries over Begg's outline, cited authorities, applications, and closing prayer material.

Full-transcript close reading found no mention of Alistair Begg, Truth For Life, or Parkside Church in any of Pat McClanahan's six reviewed sermons. The report separately records other sources that were named.

ai_writing.summary: Stylometric signals (AI-associated vocabulary, disfluency rate, essay connectives, list scaffolding, personal-anecdote markers, lexical diversity) were computed for the nine 2026 transcripts. Without a baseline of the same preacher's older sermons the numbers cannot be interpreted, so no conclusion is drawn either way.

pastors.notes: The final dependence review identifies six sermons in the series as Pat McClanahan's and two as sermons by other FBC preachers; the two comparison sermons by other preachers showed no Begg material. The 3.72% figure in the preliminary exact-eight-word-run analysis used whole-service transcripts and is not the sermon-body coverage figure. The final review segments the sermon proper, uses near-verbatim alignment plus independent close reading, and reports 10% to 40% per sermon and 27.2% across Pat McClanahan's six sermons. A same-preacher pre-2023 baseline is still needed for the separate AI-writing review.
